public_body: Soldiers' Home In Holyoke Board Of Trustees
overall: The AG found the Soldiers' Home Board violated the Open Meeting Law by holding five 2016 executive sessions to interview superintendent candidates without a valid purpose, and by withholding minutes and resumes improperly; it ordered minutes amended and released and member training.

allegations.summary: Board met in executive session to interview and discuss superintendent candidates, allegedly not as a preliminary screening committee and without the required chair statement.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board violated the Law when it entered executive session without a proper statutory purpose on February 17, February 26, March 9, March 11, and March 18, 2016.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair did not make the required statement that open discussion would harm recruiting of qualified applicants before entering executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Although we do not make a final determination as to whether the Chair made the required statement that holding discussions in open session would have a detrimental effect in obtaining qualified applicants, we note that the minutes do not reflect that the Chair made such a statement.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged candidate packets distributed during the February 17 open session could not be withheld as documents used in open session.
Board redacted executive session minutes and withheld executive session records by citing section 22(f) despite the unlawful executive sessions.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board convened in executive session on February 17, February 26, March 9, March 11, and March 18, 2016, without a valid statutory purpose, the Board may not rely on section 22(f) of the Open Meeting Law to redact or withhold those executive session minutes in any way.

allegations.summary: Executive session minutes were alleged to be inadequate; the AG found them insufficiently detailed, omitting interviews and discussion summaries and a document list, though this was not raised in the complaint.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Board’s meeting minutes fall far short of the accuracy requirement in the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant challenged withholding of candidate scoresheets, cover letters, recommendations, references and resumes under the personnel exemption in open-session materials.
allegations.key_passage: Applying that standard, we find that the Open Meeting Law exempts from disclosure the materials used during the Board’s deliberations about appointment of the Superintendent, including the candidate scoresheets, cover letters, letters of recommendation, and references, but does not exempt from disclosure the resumes of applicants.

allegations.summary: Complaint raised several additional allegations, which the AG said would not violate the Open Meeting Law even if true, including public records concerns.
allegations.key_passage: The complaint contains several additional allegations that, even if true, would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law and we therefore decline to review them.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Amend, to the best of its ability, the executive session minutes for the February 17, February 26, March 9, March 11, and March 18, 2016 meetings and release them without redactions.
Each Board member to attend an Open Meeting Law webinar or other comprehensive training and certify completion within 60 days.
